scope: All built-in English cards from the repository. Device-local custom cards and rules written during a game are not included.

provenance.wording: Exact project wording; no rewriting or analysis applied.

comparisonNote: This is an original Tipsy Trouble deck, not a copied or exhaustively mapped Drunk Pirate catalogue.

cards.title: Three-word day
cards.text: Describe your day in exactly three words. Everyone votes on the most dramatic description. Its author gives out one sip.

cards.title: An offer you can refuse
cards.text: Pick an ordinary object nearby and give it a ten-second sales pitch. If anyone wants to buy it, give out one sip. Otherwise, take one.

cards.title: Snack court
cards.text: Defend an unpopular food combination. The table votes: delicious or disaster? Join the smaller group for one sip.

cards.title: Your entrance music
cards.text: Choose the song that should play whenever you enter a room. The player on your left chooses your entrance pose. Perform the pose or take one sip.

cards.title: Super, probably
cards.text: Invent a useless superpower. The player on your right explains how it could save the world. If the table buys the explanation, you both give out one sip.

cards.title: Air designer
cards.text: Draw a familiar logo in the air with one finger. The first person to name it gives out one sip. Nobody gets it? Take one sip.

cards.title: National what day?
cards.text: Invent a holiday and its strangest tradition. Everyone who would celebrate it raises a hand. If nobody volunteers, take one sip.

cards.title: And the award goes to…
cards.text: Give the player on your left a made-up award for something kind or funny. They give a five-second acceptance speech, then choose someone to take one sip.

cards.title: Three things
cards.text: Name three things. The next player has ten seconds to explain something they all have in common. A convincing answer earns them one sip to give away; otherwise they take one.

cards.title: Packing light
cards.text: Name five things you would take to a deserted island, without using anything another player says first. The table supplies distractions. Pause for five seconds and take one sip.

cards.title: Wrong answers welcome
cards.text: The player on your right asks you three simple questions. Give a different, obviously wrong answer each time. Accidentally tell the truth? Take one sip.

cards.title: Mystery object
cards.text: Choose something you can see. Describe it without its name, colour, or usual purpose. The first person to guess it gives out one sip.

cards.title: Name the album
cards.text: If tonight were an album, what would its title be? Everyone suggests one. The table’s favourite gives out one sip.

cards.title: Very serious debate
cards.text: You and the player on your left each get ten seconds: which is better, an extra hour of sleep or an extra hour of free time? Everyone else votes. The losing side takes one sip; with two players, call it a draw.

cards.title: Mystery holiday
cards.text: Describe a real place you want to visit using only three clues. The first person to guess it gives out one sip. Reveal the answer if nobody knows it.

cards.title: Silent cinema
cards.text: Act out making your favourite meal without speaking. You have twenty seconds. Whoever guesses first gives out one sip; no correct guesses means you take one.

cards.title: Same wavelength
cards.text: Choose another player. On the count of three, each name a fruit. Match and give out one sip each. Miss and simply try again once.

cards.title: Museum of ordinary things
cards.text: Present something nearby as a priceless museum exhibit. Explain its mysterious history in two sentences. The first player to laugh takes one sip.

cards.title: Written in the stars
cards.text: Invent a constellation named after someone at the table. Describe its shape and the legend behind it. That player gives out one sip.

cards.title: Five-star nonsense
cards.text: Review an imaginary restaurant where the food is great but everything else is bizarre. Finish with a star rating. The table’s harshest critic takes one sip.

cards.title: A word with the penguin
cards.text: The player on your right interviews you as an animal they choose. Answer two questions in character. Break character and take one sip.

cards.title: Once upon a table
cards.text: Build a story around the table, one word per player. After one complete circle, you must give the story a title. Anyone who laughs during their word takes one sip.

cards.title: Patent pending
cards.text: Invent a product that solves a very minor problem in a ridiculous way. The next player names it. Everyone who would use it takes one sip.

cards.title: Welcome to the future
cards.text: Explain a smartphone to a visitor from two hundred years ago without using the words phone, internet, or computer. Let another player choose a sip for you if you slip up.

cards.title: Completely unverified
cards.text: Make up a harmless, obviously silly fact about an everyday object. Another player delivers it like a documentary narrator. First to laugh takes one sip.

cards.title: Better together
cards.text: Name two things that belong together. The next player replaces one with something unexpected and explains why the new pair works. The table decides who gives out one sip.

cards.title: Tiny job interview
cards.text: Mime a job using only your hands. The first player to guess the job gives out one sip. After twenty seconds, reveal it and move on.

cards.title: Tonight, starring…
cards.text: Introduce the table as the cast of a fictional show. Give each player a character name. The player on your left chooses someone to take one sip.

cards.title: Party forecast
cards.text: Deliver a ten-second weather forecast for the mood at the table. Include one dramatic prediction. Anyone who interrupts takes one sip.

cards.title: A pleasant surprise
cards.text: Tell someone at the table one nice thing you noticed about them. Both of you choose a third player for a shared toast; with two players, toast each other.

cards.title: Tabletop orchestra
cards.text: Tap a short rhythm. The player on your left copies it and adds one beat. Continue once around the table. The first missed beat costs one sip.

cards.title: Cheers to that
cards.text: Name one small thing worth celebrating today. Everyone may add their own. Raise a glass together and take a sip if you like.

cards.title: Royal requests
cards.text: Begin every request to another player with “Your Majesty.” Forget the royal treatment and take one sip.

cards.title: Your own narrator
cards.text: Speak about yourself in the third person. Slip back to “I” or “me” and take one sip.

cards.title: Live from the table
cards.text: Deliver everything you say in your best serious newsreader voice. Break character and take one sip.

cards.title: Any questions?
cards.text: Everything you say must be a question. Make a statement and take one sip.

cards.title: You’re on air
cards.text: Hold an imaginary microphone whenever you speak. Forget it and take one sip.

cards.title: Wait for it…
cards.text: Pause dramatically before answering any question. Rush the answer and take one sip.

cards.title: The standing ovation, seated
cards.text: Give a tiny round of applause whenever someone finishes reading a new card. Miss your cue and take one sip.

cards.title: A tip of the hat
cards.text: Tip an imaginary hat whenever you say another player’s name. Forget your manners and take one sip.

cards.title: Last call
cards.text: Raise a toast to the table, then take three sips at your own pace.

cards.title: Captain’s choice
cards.text: Give a victory speech worthy of a captain, then take five sips at your own pace.

cards.title: Small traditions
cards.text: Name a small tradition you would like this group to start. Everyone votes with a thumbs-up. If it gets unanimous support, give out one sip.

cards.title: Junior inventor
cards.text: Describe something you tried to build as a child, or invent a childhood project. The next player supplies a grand name for it and gives out one sip.

cards.title: Quietly winning
cards.text: Share a small task you finally finished, or imagine one. The table gives you a tiny cheer. Choose someone to join you for an optional sip.

cards.title: Ask the expert
cards.text: Name a harmless subject you know oddly well. The table asks one question about it. Answer it or admit defeat and take one sip.

cards.title: Wish you were here
cards.text: Describe an ordinary Tuesday in your ideal future. The next player adds one surprising detail. Give out one sip if you would keep their addition.

cards.title: Sounds familiar
cards.text: Name a sound that reminds you of home without revealing an address. Anyone who picked the same kind of sound joins you for one optional sip.

cards.title: Skill swap
cards.text: Choose a skill you admire in another player. They name a skill they would borrow from you. If either person gets stuck, the group suggests one and shares a toast.

cards.title: Five minutes off
cards.text: Describe your perfect five-minute break using exactly five words. The table counts. Use too many or too few and take one sip.

cards.title: Rain committee
cards.text: Would you rather have a tiny umbrella or enormous rain boots? Everyone chooses at once. The smaller group takes one sip; a tie means nobody does.

cards.title: An unusual election
cards.text: Everyone nominates a fictional character to run a town. Vote for the best candidate. The winning nominator gives out one sip; tied winners share that one sip.

cards.title: Breakfast parliament
cards.text: Should soup count as breakfast? Everyone votes yes or no, then one player from each side makes a sentence-long case. You decide which side gives out one sip.

cards.title: Household upgrade
cards.text: Choose between a robot that tells terrible jokes and a plant that gives advice. Reveal your choices together. Anyone alone on their side gives out one sip.

cards.title: The extra day
cards.text: Would you add an extra Friday or an extra Sunday to the week? Each side names the day. The table's favourite name earns its creator one sip to give out.

cards.title: Colour committee
cards.text: Invent a colour name for tonight. Everyone points to their favourite suggestion. The winner gives out one sip; resolve a tie with a shared toast.

cards.title: Mascot auditions
cards.text: Each player names an animal mascot for this group. Vote, excluding your own suggestion. The winner demonstrates its greeting or takes one sip.

cards.title: Luxury budget
cards.text: Everyone chooses one everyday luxury they would keep on a tiny budget. You may swap your answer after hearing the others. Anyone who swaps takes one sip.

cards.title: Letter relay
cards.text: Say an animal. Go once around the table: each new animal must start with the previous animal's last letter. The first repeat or five-second pause takes one sip, then stop.

cards.title: Missing a vowel
cards.text: Describe a beach without saying any word containing the letter A. Speak for ten seconds. If the table spots an A-word, take one sip.

cards.title: Word renovation
cards.text: Say a compound word, such as lighthouse. The next player replaces one half to make a real new word. Keep going for six links. The first player stuck takes one sip.

cards.title: The name department
cards.text: Give yourself an alias with three words starting with the same letter. The next player repeats it. If they miss a word, they take one sip; otherwise you give out one.

cards.title: Extremely short review
cards.text: Review a familiar film using two words, without its title. The table gets three guesses. If nobody solves it, reveal the film and take one sip.

cards.title: Rhyme time
cards.text: Choose a word that has several rhymes. Go around once, adding new rhymes. The first repeated rhyme or five-second pause takes one sip, and the ladder ends.

cards.title: Official nonsense
cards.text: The player on your left gives you three letters. Turn them into the name of a ridiculous organisation and explain its job. Get stuck for ten seconds and take one sip.

cards.title: One letter better
cards.text: Name a word of at least four letters. Another player changes one letter to make a new word. Make four changes together; the first invalid word costs its speaker one sip.

cards.title: One-colour menu
cards.text: Pick a colour. Go once around naming foods naturally that colour. No repeats. The first player stuck for five seconds takes one sip, then reveal the rest of your ideas.

cards.title: Rolling stock
cards.text: Name something with wheels. Continue around once without repeats, but cars and bicycles are off limits. The first invalid answer takes one sip and ends the round.

cards.title: After dark
cards.text: Go around once naming sounds you might hear at night. Each player must make their sound too. The first repeat takes one sip; unusual but plausible answers count.

cards.title: Imaginary atlas
cards.text: Name a fictional place. Go around once adding new places, without naming the same story twice. The first person who cannot answer takes one sip.

cards.title: Pocket inventory
cards.text: Name three objects that fit in a pocket but are not usually carried there. The table checks their sizes. If all three fit, give out one sip; otherwise take one.

cards.title: Weather does things
cards.text: Name something weather can do, using a verb. Continue around once without repeats. The first five-second pause takes one sip, then stop.

cards.title: Wrong department
cards.text: Name something you can stir with that is not a kitchen utensil. Each player adds a different imaginary option. The table's most impractical suggestion gives out one sip.

cards.title: Around we go
cards.text: Go around once naming round objects. Each answer must be smaller than the previous one. The first size dispute is settled by a vote; its losing speaker takes one sip.

cards.title: Very strange shopping
cards.text: Start a shopping list with one unusual item. Each player repeats the list and adds one. Stop after one circle or the first mistake; whoever makes that mistake takes one sip.

cards.title: Remember this move
cards.text: Each player makes a small hand gesture. After everyone has shown theirs, copy the gesture of the player opposite you, or your only partner. Miss it and take one sip.

cards.title: Eyes on the table
cards.text: Another player names three visible objects. Look away and repeat them in reverse order. Get all three and give out one sip; miss one and take one.

cards.title: Cast roll backwards
cards.text: Say every player's name in reverse playing order, starting with yourself. You get one restart. If you still miss someone, take one sip.

cards.title: Were you listening?
cards.text: Tell a made-up story with a colour, an animal, and a number. The next player recalls all three. If they succeed, you each give out one sip; otherwise they take one.

cards.title: The silent sequence
cards.text: Show three simple hand poses. The player on your left copies them in reverse order. A correct sequence earns them one sip to give out; otherwise they take one.

cards.title: The absent-minded waiter
cards.text: Each player orders an imaginary snack. Without notes, repeat up to five orders. Miss an order and take one sip; get them all and give out one.

cards.title: Back to the beginning
cards.text: Each player says a word. After one circle, name the first and last words spoken by other players. With two players, repeat your partner's word backwards. Miss and take one sip.

cards.title: Count us in
cards.text: As a group, count from one to ten with no fixed speaking order. If two people speak together, stop; those two each take one sip. You get one attempt.

cards.title: Mirror partners
cards.text: Face another player and mirror their slow hand movements for ten seconds while both stay seated. They choose one unexpected change. Lose track and take one sip.

cards.title: Shape agreement
cards.text: Choose another player. Without discussion, draw a shape in the air on three. Match and give out one sip together; differ and let the table name your combined shape.

cards.title: Alphabet duet
cards.text: You and the next player alternate letters from A to P. Clap instead of saying each vowel. The first person who slips takes one sip, then stop.

cards.title: Mind the gap
cards.text: Clap a steady four-beat pattern together. On the third repeat, everyone leaves the last beat silent. Anyone who claps into the gap takes one sip.

cards.title: Almost synchronised
cards.text: Choose a partner. Close your eyes while seated and count five seconds silently, then say now. If the table hears two separate calls, you both take one sip.

cards.title: Air sketch partners
cards.text: With a partner, draw an imaginary house: you describe each line while they trace it in the air. They must keep their finger moving for ten seconds. A pause costs you one sip.

cards.title: Alternating introductions
cards.text: You and the player on your right introduce an imaginary guest, alternating one word at a time. Complete one sensible sentence. If you both speak at once, take one sip each.

cards.title: Please hold
cards.text: Give a polite customer-service apology for the moon arriving late. Include a proposed refund. The table chooses the best phrase; its first person to repeat it gives out one sip.

cards.title: A very slow winner
cards.text: Celebrate winning a tiny imaginary prize in slow motion for ten seconds, staying seated. Anyone who guesses the prize gives out one sip; reveal it if nobody does.

cards.title: The object speaks
cards.text: Give a nearby object a twenty-second monologue about its day. Another player supplies its first sentence. Break character and take one sip.

cards.title: Quiet blockbuster
cards.text: Whisper a dramatic trailer for a film about doing laundry. Include a villain and a cliffhanger. The first person to laugh takes one sip.

cards.title: Hear ye, hear ye
cards.text: Announce a completely ordinary household task as a royal decree. The next player formally objects. If either uses the word boring, they take one sip.

cards.title: Live coverage
cards.text: Commentate on another player's slow imaginary sandwich-making for fifteen seconds. Invent a sporting record they might break. Run out of words and take one sip.

cards.title: Three voices
cards.text: Say the same friendly greeting as a robot, a wizard, and a tired shopkeeper. The table chooses its favourite voice. Use it to award someone one sip.

cards.title: Human appliance
cards.text: Act out an appliance using only your face and hands. The table gets three guesses. A correct guess earns one sip to give out; otherwise reveal it and take one.

cards.title: Cloud employment
cards.text: Invent a job that could exist in a city built on clouds. The next player explains its biggest workplace problem. The table awards the better idea one sip to give out.

cards.title: Pocket-sized problem
cards.text: A tiny dragon moves into your kitchen. Explain one house rule you would give it. Another player responds as the dragon. Whoever laughs first takes one sip.

cards.title: Open in one hundred years
cards.text: Choose a harmless object for a time capsule and write its imaginary warning label aloud. If anyone mistakes it for a different object, they take one sip.

cards.title: Lunar high street
cards.text: Invent a shop for the moon and its first sale. The next player is a difficult customer. Finish your two-line exchange without mentioning gravity, or take one sip.

cards.title: The visitors are on display
cards.text: Imagine a zoo where animals visit humans. Describe the sign outside your enclosure. The table adds one care instruction, then chooses someone for one sip.

cards.title: Haunted but helpful
cards.text: A friendly ghost can perform one chore badly. Choose its chore and demonstrate the problem using your hands. The table's best repair suggestion gives out one sip.

cards.title: Weather on demand
cards.text: Invent a weather subscription with a ridiculous premium feature. Pitch it in one sentence. Anyone who would subscribe raises a hand; no customers means you take one sip.

cards.title: City in a cereal box
cards.text: Design one landmark for a tiny city inside a cereal box. The next player names its mayor. Give out one sip if the mayor's name makes you smile.

cards.title: Sandwich law
cards.text: State one rule for what counts as a sandwich. The next player offers a tricky example. If your rule contradicts your answer, take one sip.

cards.title: Crunch, probably
cards.text: Make the sound of eating an imaginary snack without naming it. The first correct guess gives out one sip. After three guesses, reveal the snack and move on.

cards.title: Fancy menu decoder
cards.text: Describe toast as if it costs a fortune at a restaurant. Another player translates your description back into plain language. The shorter description gives out one sip.

cards.title: Questionable flavour lab
cards.text: Invent a new ice-cream flavour using two things that are actually edible. Everyone votes try it or leave it. If nobody would try it, take one sip.

cards.title: Picnic with a catch
cards.text: Plan a picnic where every food must begin with the same letter as your name. Name three foods or take one sip. Repeating ingredients is allowed; repeating foods is not.

cards.title: The last biscuit hearing
cards.text: Make a ten-second argument for why an imaginary last biscuit belongs to you. The next player is the judge. Accept their verdict with a bow, or take one sip.

cards.title: Soup, now with drama
cards.text: Create a five-word slogan for an ordinary soup. Everyone repeats it together. If anyone adds a word, that person takes one sip.

cards.title: The midnight special
cards.text: Everyone names a late-night snack. You must combine two suggestions into one imaginary dish and give it a name. Its two contributors share one optional sip.

cards.title: The unreliable guide
cards.text: Describe a familiar place as if your guidebook got one fact hilariously wrong. The first person to identify the invented detail gives out one sip.

cards.title: Only three things
cards.text: You have room for three items on a fictional holiday. Name them, then the next player removes one. Explain how you will cope without it or take one sip.

cards.title: Platform nonsense
cards.text: Announce a train to an impossible destination. Include a delay caused by something tiny. Anyone who smiles before you finish takes one sip.

cards.title: Island administration
cards.text: This group has founded an imaginary island. Give it a name, a flag design, and one public holiday. If any detail repeats another player's earlier idea tonight, take one sip.

cards.title: Wish you were somewhere
cards.text: The player on your left names a place. Give a postcard message that could apply there or in a supermarket. A convincing message earns you one sip to give out.

cards.title: The local landmark
cards.text: Pose with your face and hands as an imaginary statue while seated. The next player explains what it commemorates. The first person to break a straight face takes one sip.

cards.title: One peculiar star
cards.text: Review a fictional hotel with one excellent feature and one absurd inconvenience. The group rates it from one to five using fingers. The highest rating gives out one sip; ties share it.

cards.title: Alphabet itinerary
cards.text: Plan three imaginary stops whose initials spell a three-letter word. Explain your route. If the table cannot identify the word, reveal it and take one sip.

cards.title: The song description
cards.text: Describe a familiar song without singing, humming, or quoting lyrics. Give three clues. The first correct guess gives out one sip; no guess means you take one.

cards.title: A grand entrance
cards.text: Compose a three-note doorbell sound using your voice. The table echoes it once. The player whose version you would install gives out one sip.

cards.title: Name that beat
cards.text: Tap the rhythm of your full name on your knees while seated. The next player answers with theirs. If the rhythms match, share an optional sip.

cards.title: Wrong soundtrack
cards.text: Choose music for a dramatic scene, then replace it with the least suitable genre you can imagine. Describe the result. The table's first laugh takes one sip.

cards.title: Band meeting
cards.text: You are forming a band. Assign the next three players, or as many as available, imaginary instruments. They each make one sound. Name the band and give out one sip.

cards.title: Eight-second advert
cards.text: Invent an eight-second jingle for a household object. You may speak rhythmically instead of singing. Forget to name the object and take one sip.

cards.title: Indoor voice detective
cards.text: Say one sentence in three different moods at the same quiet volume. The table identifies the moods. For each missed mood, reveal it; if all three are missed, take one sip.

cards.title: The rhythm parcel
cards.text: Tap twice, then point to another player. They tap twice and choose someone new. Continue until everyone has played. The first extra tap costs one sip.

cards.title: Spoil it backwards
cards.text: Describe a familiar story backwards in three sentences, without names. The table gets one guess per player. The first correct guess gives out one sip.

cards.title: The unnecessary sequel
cards.text: Invent a sequel to an ordinary chore. Give it a dramatic title and a one-sentence plot. Everyone votes watch or skip; if nobody would watch, take one sip.

cards.title: A very important extra
cards.text: Describe a film scene from the perspective of an unnoticed background character. The next player guesses the genre. Agree with the guess and give out one sip; disagree and take one.

cards.title: Judge this cover
cards.text: Invent a book title from the last object you touched and the current weather. The next player supplies its opening sentence. If the group wants chapter two, give out one sip.

cards.title: Genre collision
cards.text: Tell a three-sentence story: first a mystery, then a romance, then science fiction. The table supplies your main character's name. Miss a genre and take one sip.

cards.title: One essential prop
cards.text: Name an ordinary object. The next player invents a film scene that makes it crucial. You have one sentence to explain its unexpected sequel appearance, or take one sip.

cards.title: Choose the ending
cards.text: Begin a story in two sentences. The next two players, or your only partner and you, each suggest an ending. Vote for one; its author gives out one sip.

cards.title: Coming eventually
cards.text: Give a serious trailer voiceover for tomorrow's breakfast. Use exactly three sentences. The table counts; the wrong number costs one sip.

cards.title: Behind the scenes
cards.text: Name a small helpful thing someone at the table has done, or might do well. That person chooses someone else to thank. End with an optional shared sip.

cards.title: A slightly odd compliment
cards.text: Compliment another player by comparing them to a useful object. Explain the comparison kindly. They may accept with an imaginary medal or return a compliment.

cards.title: Collective talent
cards.text: Name a task this group could do surprisingly well together. Assign everyone a role. Anyone who wants a different role must pitch it in five words or take one sip.

cards.title: Some good news
cards.text: Give a fifteen-second news bulletin about three tiny positive things, real or invented. If you repeat a topic, take one sip; otherwise give out one.

cards.title: Next year's headline
cards.text: Invent a positive headline about the player on your right one year from now. They give a short response. Both of you choose someone for an optional toast.

cards.title: Pass something good
cards.text: Each player names one small kindness someone could do tomorrow. No repeats. If an idea has already been said, offer a new one or take one sip.

cards.title: The group project
cards.text: Choose a harmless imaginary project for the group. Everyone contributes one idea. You have ten seconds to combine up to three of those ideas into a plan, or take one sip.

cards.title: A party for almost nothing
cards.text: Plan a celebration using only things already in this room, without moving or using them. The table votes on the best detail. Its creator gives out one sip.

cards.title: Advice in reverse
cards.text: Give obviously terrible advice for keeping a houseplant alive. The next player converts it into useful advice. If either accidentally gives the wrong kind, take one sip.

cards.title: Hands off the explanation
cards.text: Explain how to wrap a present without moving your hands. The next player watches for gestures. A gesture costs one sip; a clean explanation earns one to give out.

cards.title: The missing spoon
cards.text: Give a nearby object an alibi for an imaginary missing spoon. Another player asks one follow-up question. Contradict yourself and take one sip.

cards.title: Instruction manual
cards.text: Explain how to use an umbrella to someone who thinks it is a musical instrument. You cannot say rain or wet. Use either word and take one sip.

cards.title: Small, medium, surprising
cards.text: Another player names three objects. Put them in size order, then invent a situation where the order reverses. If the table accepts the explanation, give out one sip.

cards.title: A third option
cards.text: The player on your left offers two ordinary choices. Invent a sensible third option that combines both. If the table cannot see both parts, take one sip.

cards.title: Five-question mystery
cards.text: Think of an everyday object. The table may ask five yes-or-no questions, then make one shared guess. If correct, you take one sip; otherwise give out one.

cards.title: Prove the obvious
cards.text: Explain why a chair is definitely not a sandwich, without using the words sit, bread, or eat. Use a forbidden word and take one sip.

cards.title: Season forecast
cards.text: Privately choose a favourite season. Everyone points to someone and predicts theirs. Reveal in playing order. Each incorrect predictor takes one sip.

cards.title: Meet in the middle
cards.text: Everyone chooses a number from one to five and reveals it with fingers together. Anyone whose number matches yours gives out one sip; if nobody matches, you take one.

cards.title: Snack forecast
cards.text: Guess the next player's choice between sweet, salty, and sour before they answer. A correct guess earns you one sip to give out; a wrong guess costs one sip.

cards.title: What colour is Monday?
cards.text: Everyone secretly decides what colour Monday would be. Reveal together. If any answers match, those players give out one sip together; otherwise the table shares a toast.

cards.title: Roommate shortlist
cards.text: Name two fictional characters. Predict which one the next player would prefer as a roommate. They reveal their choice and one reason. Guess wrong and take one sip.

cards.title: Predict the punchline
cards.text: Start an invented sentence with Tomorrow I will definitely. The next player privately chooses an ending; predict its first word. Match and give out three sips, shared among volunteers.

cards.title: One-object weekend
cards.text: Think of an object that represents your ideal weekend. Give its colour as a clue. The table gets three guesses. A correct guess gives out one sip; otherwise reveal it.

cards.title: Empty-handed guess
cards.text: Put an imaginary coin in either closed hand and choose honestly. Another player guesses which hand. A wrong guess costs them one sip; a correct guess costs you one.

cards.title: Find the connection
cards.text: Name something visible in the room. The next player names something else and explains a connection in one sentence. Continue for four links; the first repeat takes one sip.

cards.title: Map of the room
cards.text: Describe this room as an imaginary country. Give three landmarks playful names. The first player to identify all three real locations gives out one sip.

cards.title: Chair of the committee
cards.text: Nominate three visible objects for an imaginary committee. Everyone votes on its chairperson. Give the winning object a one-sentence acceptance speech, or take one sip.

cards.title: Know your neighbours
cards.text: Without looking, name one visible colour worn by the player on each side. With two players, name two colours your partner wears. If either is wrong, take one sip.

cards.title: Freeze-frame caption
cards.text: Make a harmless seated pose with your hands and face. Everyone supplies a caption. Choose your favourite; its author gives out one sip.

cards.title: Find a connection
cards.text: Find one harmless preference shared by every player using no more than five questions. Succeed and give out three sips among volunteers; otherwise offer a shared toast.

cards.title: The room has an answer
cards.text: Make a two-line riddle about something visible nearby, without naming its colour. The first player to solve it gives out one sip. Reveal the answer after three guesses.

cards.title: Until the next card
cards.text: Give a ten-second farewell speech to the card you are reading. Include one sincere compliment about its punctuation. If you laugh before finishing, take one sip.

cards.title: Over and out
cards.text: End each conversational reply with “over.” Forget your radio sign-off and take one sip.

cards.title: A formal address
cards.text: Before asking someone a question, introduce yourself with your full first name. Forget the introduction and take one sip.

cards.title: Beyond yes and no
cards.text: In conversation, answer without using the words yes or no. Say either word and take one sip.

cards.title: Forecast included
cards.text: Whenever someone asks how you are, answer with a weather forecast for your mood. Give an ordinary answer and take one sip.

cards.title: Taking notes
cards.text: When another player gives you a direct instruction, mime noting it in a little notebook. Forget your notes and take one sip.

cards.title: Opening night
cards.text: Before reading a new card aloud, mime opening a tiny curtain with your hands. Miss the opening and take one sip.

cards.title: Pardon the interruption
cards.text: If you interrupt another player, immediately say “please continue” and let them finish. Forget the phrase and take one sip.

cards.title: Just to confirm
cards.text: Repeat the last word of any question addressed to you before answering it. Skip the echo and take one sip.

cards.title: Names off duty
cards.text: Use friendly descriptions instead of players' names during conversation. Say a player's name and take one sip. Reading names printed on a card is allowed.

cards.title: A gracious reply
cards.text: Give a small seated nod whenever another player thanks you. Miss the acknowledgment and take one sip.

cards.title: Punctuation unit
cards.text: Say “full stop” after each conversational statement and “question mark” after each question. Miss the punctuation and take one sip.

cards.title: A useful word
cards.text: Whenever you say “actually” in conversation, immediately add “and that is official.” Forget the addition and take one sip.

cards.title: Looking ahead
cards.text: When talking about yourself in conversation, describe what you will do rather than what you did. Slip into your own past and take one sip.

cards.title: Credit where due
cards.text: Whenever you receive a compliment, thank the whole table by saying “team effort.” Forget the phrase and take one sip.

cards.title: Someone at the door
cards.text: Before asking the whole group a question, say “ding-dong” once. Forget the doorbell and take one sip.

cards.title: Count it out
cards.text: Whenever you mention a number from one to five in conversation, show it with your fingers too. Forget the matching fingers and take one sip.

cards.title: According to my research
cards.text: Begin explanations of how something works with “according to my research.” Forget your scholarly opening and take one sip.

cards.title: The open-hand policy
cards.text: Indicate people and objects with an open hand rather than one pointing finger. Point with a finger and take one sip.

cards.title: I'll ask my assistant
cards.text: Before giving an opinion, briefly consult an imaginary assistant beside you. Forget the consultation and take one sip.

cards.title: A small announcement
cards.text: Before announcing a decision, make a quiet two-note fanfare. Forget the fanfare and take one sip.

cards.title: Compliment received
cards.text: When someone compliments you, mime placing the compliment safely in a pocket. Forget to keep it and take one sip.

cards.title: We have an opinion
cards.text: Use “we” instead of “I” when sharing your own opinions. Slip back into the singular and take one sip.

cards.title: Quote, unquote
cards.text: When quoting something another person said, make small quotation marks with your fingers. Forget the gesture and take one sip.

cards.title: Hello again
cards.text: Whenever you say hello or goodbye, add a small wave with your left hand. Miss the wave and take one sip.

cards.title: Post-match interview
cards.text: Begin answers to personal questions with “it was a team effort.” Forget the interview phrase and take one sip.

cards.title: Let me examine that
cards.text: Before reading anything aloud, adjust a pair of imaginary spectacles. Forget your spectacles and take one sip.

cards.title: Chef's compliments
cards.text: Whenever you name a food in conversation, call it “the magnificent” food. For example, the magnificent toast. Forget its title and take one sip.

cards.title: A moment of thought
cards.text: Touch your chin briefly before answering a question about your preferences. Forget your thoughtful pose and take one sip.

cards.title: Audible approval
cards.text: Add a quiet “ta-da” whenever you agree to a suggestion. Forget your sound effect and take one sip.

cards.title: All in favour
cards.text: When a card asks the group to vote, wait for the current player to say “polls open.” Vote before that announcement and take one sip.
